# Hallmark Design Skill for Muse

An opinionated anti-"AI slop" design skill for AI coding assistants: it makes generated UIs look made, not generated. One default behaviour (design a new page) and two verbs that fire only when you name Hallmark: `hallmark audit` of a target (read-only punch list) and `hallmark redesign` (a full redesign that keeps the target's content and wiring). It enforces structural variety (21 named macrostructures, 48 themes dealt by a bundled script with a rotation log so two builds never look alike), a gate system (a 16-rule non-waivable Floor, waivable Reflex gates and Finish checks, in references/gates.md) enforced by the bundled sloplint script with rendered screenshots before hand-back, honest-copy rules (no invented metrics or testimonials), locked design tokens, and an 8-state discipline for interactive components. It reads your project first (pre-flight), then asks once, in a single message (material, audience, use case, tone), so it never stomps on an existing palette or font stack. Discovered via skills.sh. Honest note: it carries a "Powered by Together AI" credit line in the intro — the skill's content is pure design methodology and needs no paid service; a TOGETHER_API_KEY, if you set one, optionally enables a generated-comp step. This is aimed at anyone building web pages with an AI assistant, not just developers.
